Our jobs aren’t just about putting food on the table that our guests will enjoy until they ask for their bill. Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique – with food and drinks on the side. Our Guest Service Support Experts take the initiative and deliver a wide range of services to make sure food and beverage operations run smoothly. Whether setting tables, assisting the kitchen, or cleaning work areas and replenishing supplies, the Guest Service Support Expert provides the support that make transactions feel like part of the experience.

No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – creating a safe workplace, following company policies and procedures, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Guest Service Support Experts will be on their feet and moving around (stand, sit, or walk for an extended time; moving over sloping, uneven, or slippery surfaces), managing the menu (read and visually verify information), and taking a hands-on approach to work (move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 25 pounds without assistance and 50 pounds with assistance; reach overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping). Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for Guest Service Support Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time.
q: Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent.
Related Work Experience: No related work experience. Previous experience in a food and beverage environment preferred.

q: 15 years’ experience in Offshore Process Safety

r: Has demonstrated experience in Process Safety. Knowledge of project engineering practices, international codes, standards, procedures, and specifications.
Developing and checking of calculations, data sheets, technical notes, requisitions, specifications, drawings and similar deliverables produced within Discipline.

d: Build and own one integrated schedule per destination that links design, approvals, procurement, construction, sales handovers and hotel/amenity openings, and give management an early, honest read on delivery risk.

The position is at the Muriya's Projects / Development Directorate and serve integrated tourism complexes (ITCs) where residential, hospitality, F&B, retail, marinas and destination infrastructure are delivered in parallel phases at Jebel Sifah, Hawana Salalah and future destinations.
What makes Muriya different from a contractor or a single-asset developer, and what candidates must be screened for:
High cross-functionality: every project decision touches Sales, Finance, Destination/Community Management, Hotel Operators, Legal, Procurement and Government Relations at once.

Owner-side, not contractor-side: the roles manage consultants and contractors, protect the employer's interests, and translate commercial targets (sales handovers, hotel openings, season readiness) into delivery dates.
Live destinations: construction happens next to residents, guests and operating hotels, so phasing, logistics, HSE and brand experience are part of the job.
Omani regulatory environment: ITC framework under the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism, municipal and Civil Defense approvals, environmental permits (EA), Omanisation and ICV requirements.
Multi-site, coastal and remote: Muscat (Jebel Sifah) and Dhofar (Hawana Salalah, khareef season constraints) with travel between sites.
q: BSc in a construction-related engineering or construction management discipline.
5 years (±) planning experience; real estate, hospitality, mixed-use or infrastructure projects.
Advanced Primavera P6; strong Excel; Power BI or similar for dashboards.
Working knowledge of FIDIC contracts, EOT and delay analysis.
Fluent English; Arabic is an advantage.
PMI-SP (Scheduling Professional), PMP or AACE PSP.
Exposure to owner/developer side, not only contractor side.
Experience with Synchro 4D, Aconex/ACC or other CDE platforms.
Communicates schedule messages in plain business terms to non-technical teams.
Challenges contractors and internal teams on dates with evidence, not opinion.
Comfortable working across departments without direct authority.
Detail-driven, but keeps the destination-level picture in view.
r: Develop and maintain Level 1–4 schedules (master program to detailed works) in Primavera P6 for each destination and project.
Build the integrated master schedule that ties construction milestones to sales handover commitments, operator pre-opening timelines and destination events.
Define WBS, activity coding and resource/cost loading in line with Muriya's project controls standards.
Establish and control baselines; manage schedule revisions through formal change control.
Review contractor baseline and updated programs against contract requirements (FIDIC, local conditions) and recommend acceptance or rejection.
Assess extension-of-time claims and prepare time-impact and delay analyses (TIA, windows, as-planned vs as-built).
Verify progress on site; reconcile reported progress with physical progress and payment applications.
Track progress with earned value (SPI, CPI), critical path and float erosion; flag slippage early with recovery options.
Produce weekly and monthly progress reports and dashboards for the Projects Director, Executive Management and Board.
Maintain look-ahead programs (3-week / 3-month) and coordinate interfaces between multiple contractors on shared sites.
Feed delivery dates to Sales & Marketing for launch, handover and customer communications; flag risks to promised handover dates.
Align with Finance on cash-flow forecasts, budget phasing and capex S-curves.
Coordinate with Hotel Operators and Destination Management on pre-opening, FF&E, OS&E and testing & commissioning windows.
Track authority approvals (Municipality, Civil Defense, Environment Authority, utilities) and their impact on critical path.
Plan works around live destination operations, peak seasons and khareef in Dhofar.
Support the risk register with schedule risk analysis (Monte Carlo / QSRA) for major projects.
Capture lessons learned and improve planning templates and standards across destinations.
Schedule reporting: Monthly report issued by working day 5; weekly updates every week
Forecast accuracy: Milestone forecast within ±4 weeks of actual at 3 months out
Contractor programme reviews: Turned around within 10 working days
EOT / delay assessments: Substantiated and issued within contractual timeframes
Early warning: Critical-path slippage flagged within one reporting cycle, with recovery options
Stakeholder alignment: Sales, Finance and Operations working from the same milestone dates
